clue.text: See 11
Composer's brother, another with no daughter

parts.note: sib is short for sibling, a brother or sister

indicators.note: with no tells us to drop a letter from the other composer's name

parts.note: another composer, Frederick Delius

explanation.surface: A question about a composer's brother and some other musician who had no daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes D from DELIUS, leaving ELIUS. The 's of 'Composer's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was the great Finnish symphonist who wrote Finlandia.

clue.text: Uneasy lies Britain, perhaps

indicators.note: uneasy suggests the letters are unsettled and so rearranged

explanation.surface: The opening of Shakespeare's line about a restless king, applied to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uneasy' rearranges LIES. The words also begin the quotation completed at 11 and 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is an example of an island, signalled by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Stopped wild deer chasing mate

indicators.note: chasing means the rearranged letters come after, following behind

parts.note: a hind is a female deer, the mate of a stag

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the word run riot and rearrange

explanation.surface: A hunter's tale of wild deer pursuing a partner, then halting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' anagrams the deer, and 'chasing' sets that after the mate; the deer in the surface is not the hind.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hindered is to be obstructed or held back, roughly stopped.

clue.text: Fix one to race with a companion

parts.note: one is the article A
TT, Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorbike race
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Instructions for joining a race with a partner beside you.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man; CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something in place is to attach or fasten it.

clue.text: See 26
See 26
Vast your skill, reportedly being beyond our reckoning

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.note: vast gives IMMENSE, your stays YOUR, skill gives ABILITY

explanation.surface: A compliment that someone's talent is so great it cannot be measured.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'immense your ability' runs together into the long abstract noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Immensurability is the quality of being too great to be measured or counted.

clue.text: Uncomfortable wear, deerskin, for Irish vagrant

indicators.note: for means the deer's skin serves as a cover for what goes inside

parts.note: a hart is a male deer, here acting as a skin round other letters

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A deerskin garment is made for a wandering Irishman, and it chafes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' anagrams the Irish, and 'for' has the deer serve as a skin round it; a hart is a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse penitential garment worn next to the skin as self-mortification.

clue.text: House with sound of activity that's boring

parts.note: a hum is the busy sound of activity, as of a hive

explanation.surface: A house buzzing with activity, yet tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum is an expression of weary indifference, describing something dull.

clue.text: He had no rest, a w-watcher at play

definitions.text: He had no rest, a w-watcher at play

indicators.note: at play means the letters are moved about freely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stammering king, sleepless, watched over as if at a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges HE HAD NO REST A W WATCHER AT. It completes 3's 'Uneasy lies', Henry IV Part 2's line about a sleepless king.
explanation.definitionFit: The crowned monarch in Shakespeare's line cannot sleep for worry, matching having no rest.

clue.text: Fit man, a model one, without handicap

parts.note: T as in the Model T Ford

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round another

parts.note: he means one, a person
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A fit model is described as having no disability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. LET as a hindrance survives in British passports' 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a sportsperson, a physically fit man or woman.

clue.text: The wrong way to be

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist

explanation.surface: A moral judgement on how not to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wrong way' turns LIVE round, and the whole clue also describes wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness is the wrong way to exist, the sense the whole clue gives.

clue.text: Homes for Chinese in Yellow Pages

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: in means the Chinese people are placed inside the word pages

parts.note: taken as written
the Han are the majority Chinese people

explanation.surface: Looking up Chinese homes in the telephone directory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' slips the Chinese people into the pages after the first letter. Heraldry calls gold or yellow 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's homes for those without parents are institutions that house orphans.

clue.text: Answer to where engineers keep fish?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, here possessive
a pond is where people keep fish

explanation.surface: A question about where military engineers store fish.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; their pond is the RE'S POND.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, to give an answer.

clue.text: Umpire's finger correctly raised? Absolutely

definitions.meaning: in cricket an umpire raises a finger to give a batsman out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the umpire raises one finger to signal a batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely or wholly, the same as absolutely.

clue.text: One demonstrating to get number on sign in English

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals
Sagittarius, the zodiac sign, is the Archer in English

explanation.surface: A protester gets a placard with a figure on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sagittarius is the zodiac sign whose English name is the Archer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marcher is someone walking in a protest, a demonstrator.

clue.text: Characteristic of tough guy, son of his doctor?

parts.note: Mac in Gaelic surnames means son of
taken as written
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hard man's trait came from his doctor's son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son of' wants to be S; it is MAC, the Gaelic prefix in surnames such as MacDonald.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is aggressive masculine pride, the hallmark of a tough guy.

clue.text: As a volunteer and not in white?

indicators.note: in means the word for and-not sits inside the word for white

parts.note: hoary means white or grey with age
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A question whether volunteering means being without a white uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the conjunction inside the word for white; 'and' and 'not' look like links but together are the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary role is unpaid, done voluntarily without salary.

clue.text: Entry to a ball holding hand

indicators.note: holding means the dance word wraps round the hand word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Gaining entry to a ball while holding someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' wraps the ball round the hand, which goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is permission to enter, an entry.

clue.text: Sufi, say, suffers setter's endless criticism

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says my

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the word

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism

explanation.surface: A Muslim holy man puts up with the crossword setter's criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the K from STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is an example of a mystic, a seeker of union with God.

clue.text: Herbal remedy of Carian origin

indicators.note: the remedy's origin lies in rearranging the letters of the word given

explanation.surface: A herbal cure that comes from ancient Caria in Asia Minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin' rearranges CARIAN; Caria was a region of ancient Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a plant-based ointment used on bruises and sprains.

clue.text: Rebuff turned up

definitions.meaning: to rebuff is to rebuff or slight someone pointedly
a turned-up nose is short and tilted upward

explanation.definitionFit: A snub is a pointed slight, and a snub nose is turned up at the tip.

clue.text: German decapitated by neighbour

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a Prussian was a German from Prussia

explanation.surface: A German is beheaded by the man next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' drops the P from PRUSSIAN. Read it as 'neighbour decapitates German', in the passive.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia borders Germany's former eastern lands, so a native is a neighbour.

clue.text: Risk of empire losing article

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: imperial means of an empire
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An empire risks losing an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes A from IMPERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it at risk or in danger.

clue.text: Advertisement for half steam train

indicators.note: half means only the first of the two equal parts is taken

parts.note: ...-... is a child's word for a steam train

explanation.surface: Advertising cheap half fares on a steam railway.
explanation.walkthrough: A puff-puff is British nursery talk for a steam train.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a piece of exaggerated promotional praise, an advert.

clue.text: Original question that led model couple of men to Pole, for example with repeated letters

parts.note: which can replace that as a relative pronoun
led means came first, went in front
T as in the Model T Ford

indicators.note: couple of means two of the same piece

parts.note: he is a man
the North Pole
for example is EG, and each letter is doubled

explanation.surface: A model couple of men are led to the Pole, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple of' doubles HE. EG doubled letter by letter is EEGG.
explanation.definitionFit: The age-old riddle about origins: did the bird or its egg exist first.

clue.text: See 26
